strings.title: A Seal After Closing
strings.hint: Do not correct the times using a suspect’s claim. You have one event recorded by two devices.
strings.solvedText:
The culprit is Qais Jaber, the deputy director.

Qais did not need a stopped clock. He needed everyone to read the wrong one.

1. Both tests in 30-E2 establish that the corridor camera is eight minutes ahead of the reference clock, not fifteen as he claimed. Subtract 8 minutes from 30-E1: Lama entered at 19:29:00 and left at 19:40:00; Qais entered at 19:40:40 and left at 19:45:10; the cleaner entered at 19:47:00.

2. The live call in 30-E3 ended at 19:42:30. Marwan was alive then and was found dead at 19:47. Qais’s presence in reception from 19:46 does not cover the start of that interval. His false correction would place his departure at 19:38:10; the verified correction places it after the call.

3. The sole entrance in 30-D1 and continuous footage in 30-E1 place Qais alone with Marwan inside the wing during the assault window. Lama was in reception from 19:40:30; Maher was with Huda from 19:41 to 19:48; Hisham was continuously present on the western station’s video call during those same minutes. Report 30-R1 rules out an accidental fall. The assault occurred between 19:42:30 and 19:45:10; no more precise second is established.

4. The 18:10 attachments were white. The pink sheet was printed during the minute 19:41, after its saved revision at 19:41:20. The edge in 30-E5 matches the torn strip in 30-E4. Reception retained custody of the blue folder from handover onward. A folder supposedly closed since 18:10 cannot account for that new original.

5. Record 30-D3 shows Qais approved changing the beneficiary for property 218 to Al-Sanad, a company in which his wife holds a share. Marwan suspended approval because authorization was missing. Qais confronted and killed him, removed the page and hid it among his attachments before establishing a public presence in reception. Motive supports the timeline and custody evidence; it does not replace them.

Why not Lama? She lied to conceal taking her brother’s file, but 30-E7 concerns a separate request from 2023. Her departure and continuous presence in reception precede the live call. Hisham made an error and threatened to escalate it, but his video call rules out his leaving. Maher’s key opens the same filmed entrance, and his presence at the panel covers the murder window.

Qais’s later suggestion that Marwan added the sheet does not explain its removal from the binder, nor produce another person who could have committed the assault within the continuous footage. The solution rests on evidence available before the accusation, not on a new confession.

Eight minutes put him back in the wing. A pink sheet put his administrative folder back at the desk it had been taken from. The stamp remained on the torn strip, with a missing page to testify to.
strings.summary.text:
“A stamp proves that a page passed through here. It cannot tell you whose hand carried it out.”

At 19:47, the cleaner entered the reconciliation office at the municipal records building. Review chief Marwan Shehab lay behind his desk. The eastern district’s compensation file was open at a torn page. His cash, phone and watch were untouched. No door had been forced, and the power had remained on.

The deputy director says he left before the victim’s last call, relying on his interpretation of the camera clock. An archivist conceals a file she took. A surveyor insists Marwan expected him to correct “just one name.”

Before midnight, the original schedule must reach an independent committee. Its final signatory will not be there.

12 June 2025 — all times use the 24-hour clock. The timeline below uses reception’s reference; corridor camera times remain as displayed, pending comparison.
strings.summary.victim.name: Marwan Shehab
strings.summary.victim.note: He refused to approve photocopies when originals were available. He was reviewing three separate objections; none should automatically be assumed to explain his death.
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: End of a documented call with the committee clerk.
strings.scene.address: Municipal records building — eastern wing — reconciliation office
strings.scene.intro: The wing contains a waiting room, reconciliation office and file store. Its sole entrance from reception is continuously filmed by the corridor camera. The office window has intact old iron bars. The door does not lock automatically and was found ajar.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Office after removal of the body; the binder is open and the chair turned toward the door.
strings.scene.photos[1].cap: Eastern wing entrance from reception; there is no second entrance.
strings.scene.notes[0]: A brass stamp holder lies on the floor; a pink paper strip remains in the binder rings.
strings.scene.notes[1]: The water has not spilled; cash, phone and watch remain in place.
strings.scene.notes[2]: The photograph does not establish the time of death. The camera records entry into the wing, not the office interior.
strings.evidence[0].title: Eastern wing entrance recording
strings.evidence[0].desc:
Movement log extracted from the continuous original recording. These are uncorrected camera-display times:

Lama: entry 19:37:00 — exit 19:48:00.
Qais: entry 19:48:40 — exit 19:53:10.
Cleaner: entry 19:55:00.

Apart from Qais’s movements listed above, nobody else crosses the entrance between Lama’s departure and the cleaner’s arrival. No footage is missing. Consult 30-E2 before converting these times to reception’s reference.
strings.evidence[1].title: Two lamp-test records
strings.evidence[1].desc:
Each test records one event on two devices:

First test — reception reference 19:20:00; camera frame showing the lit lamp 19:28:00.
Second test — reception reference 19:52:00; camera frame 20:00:00.

Reception’s reference matched the telephone exchange clock at the start and end of the shift, within two seconds. The technician did not alter the camera clock during inspection.
strings.evidence[2].title: The last call
strings.evidence[2].desc:
From 19:41:48 to 19:42:30 on the verified reference clock.

The audio is continuous. Rana asks questions and Marwan answers immediately. He has the latest version and one beneficiary remains unsupported. The call ends normally. Nobody in the room is named, and there is no indication of a scheduled call or prerecorded audio.

This exhibit contains a certified transcript and call log; no audio file is attached.
strings.evidence[3].title: The torn pink strip
strings.evidence[3].desc:
A pink strip remains in the binder rings, carrying part of a stamp: “VERIFIED COPY — 19:41.” The rest of the page is missing from the binder.

The only paper copy of this revision came from the office printer during the minute 19:41; the day’s other copies are white and carry an older revision. Compare print log 30-D2 and the attachment examination in 30-E5.
strings.evidence[4].title: Folded attachment in the blue folder
strings.evidence[4].desc:
Qais handed the blue folder to the receptionist at 19:46. It remained in her custody without passing to anyone else and was secured after the alarm.

Among the white attachments is a folded pink sheet. Examination establishes a physical match between its torn edge and the strip in 30-E4. It bears a beneficiary correction for property 218 and Marwan’s handwritten objection. It carries neither blood nor a killer’s name.

The edge match is an examination finding, not an inference from paper color alone.
strings.evidence[5].title: Reception movements
strings.evidence[5].desc:
Presence log from the reception camera, synchronized with the reference:

Qais (30-S1): 19:46 to 19:50.
Lama (30-S2): arrives at 19:40:30 and remains until police arrive.
Maher (30-S4) and Huda (30-W2): at the alarm panel from 19:41 to 19:48.

None leaves reception during the interval stated for them. Presence after a given time does not establish a person’s earlier location.
strings.evidence[6].title: The older correction file
strings.evidence[6].desc: A request dating to 2023 concerns Lama’s brother. It is unrelated to property 218. The morning inventory photograph establishes its position in the archive before she took it. Its presence establishes administrative misconduct, not the murderer’s identity.
strings.evidence[7].title: The brass stamp holder
strings.evidence[7].desc: The holder’s shape is consistent with the injury in 30-R1. Overlapping traces cannot identify its last user. It normally stood on Marwan’s desk and was used by several employees. No isolated fingerprint resolves the case.
strings.suspects[0].name: Qais Jaber
strings.suspects[0].alibi: Claims the camera is fifteen minutes fast and that he left before the last call. Appeared in reception at 19:46.
strings.suspects[0].statement:
Q: When did you leave?
A: “At 19:53 by your camera. But it runs fifteen minutes fast. I was gone before his last call. At 19:46 I handed over my papers in reception. That is on camera.”

Q: Why carry the blue folder?
A: “Administrative attachments Marwan gave me at ten past six. I did not open it afterward.”

Q: Did you enter the office?
A: “I only stood in the waiting room. I do not recall him calling me in.”

Q: What was the disagreement?
A: “Errors in property numbering. The technical problem belongs to the surveyor, not the deputy director.”

Investigator’s note: Marwan challenged Qais’s approvals, potentially delaying his promotion. This is a possible motive, not proof. See supplement 30-D4.
strings.suspects[1].name: Lama Hilal
strings.suspects[1].alibi: Initially denied entering after seven, then admitted taking her brother’s file. Says Marwan was alive when she left.
strings.suspects[1].statement:
Q: Did you enter after seven?
A: “No.”

Q: Why were you seen at the entrance?
A: “I went to retrieve something. I do not want my brother dragged into this.”

Q: What was it?
A: “An old correction request about his house. I took it without permission. I know that was wrong, but it is not tonight’s compensation schedule.”

Q: When did you last see Marwan?
A: “He was alive behind his desk when I left. I did not look at the office clock.”

Investigator’s note: Her family-file access had been revoked over a conflict of interest. Separate misconduct does not establish murder.
strings.suspects[2].name: Hisham Radi
strings.suspects[2].alibi: Says he explained maps to the committee on a video call from the western survey station.
strings.suspects[2].statement:
Q: Where were you?
A: “At the western survey station, explaining maps to the committee over a video call.”

Q: Did you alter the boundaries?
A: “I transferred markers from an old plan. I failed to check properly, yes. But changing a beneficiary’s name is not my job.”

Q: Why write: I will not take the blame alone?
A: “They want whoever drew the final line to carry the entire chain’s mistake.”

Investigator’s note: Marwan requested an investigation into altered boundaries on two plots. See call verification 30-D5.
strings.suspects[3].name: Maher Abdoun
strings.suspects[3].relation: Holds a key to the wing
strings.suspects[3].alibi: Says he remained with the alarm technician at reception’s panel from 19:41 to 19:48.
strings.suspects[3].statement:
Q: Where were you?
A: “With the alarm technician at reception’s panel from 19:41 to 19:48.”

Q: Can you use a service passage?
A: “There is no other entrance. My key opens the same door your camera films.”

Q: Was the camera broken?
A: “The picture was fine. The clock has been confusing for a week. I do not know whether it is fast or slow.”

Investigator’s note: Marwan recommended suspension after he let a contractor use the key after hours. Possession does not establish use that evening.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Rana Afif
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I called Marwan from the recorded office line. He was turning a page and said he had the latest version, but one beneficiary remained unsupported. I asked about an entry and he answered immediately. We ended normally. I heard neither a person’s name nor an argument.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Huda Kamal
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I fitted a test lamp in the corridor and activated it twice from reception’s panel. I recorded the main screen’s time and photographed the corridor recorder on both occasions. I did not touch its clock settings. Maher was beside me from 19:41 to 19:48; we completed the second test at 19:52.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Naguib Fouad
strings.witnesses[2].statement: I arrived with my trolley on schedule. The door was ajar and Marwan was on the floor. I called to reception without touching the binder. Lama was there arguing with the clerk about a paper she had taken.
strings.folders[0].name: Scene inspection
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: 30-D1 — Access plan
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: The eastern wing is accessible only through the filmed entrance. Inspection found no recent opening in the window bars or frames. Both the waiting room and reconciliation office lie beyond that entrance; the camera establishes entry into the wing, not a particular room. An ordinary walk from the western survey station to the eastern entrance takes three minutes. All other corridors lead to reception.
strings.folders[1].name: Original records
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: 30-D2 — Printing and revision log
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body:
18:10 — White administrative attachments printed and handed to Qais.

19:41:20 — Last automatically saved page before printing: “Property 218 — beneficiary changed from the Abdel-Salam heirs to Al-Sanad — authorization document missing.”

19:41 — A single revision printed on pink paper: one page, locally from Marwan’s computer. The printer log records minutes only; printing followed the saved revision within that same minute.

No other pink copy was printed, and this version was not emailed before the alarm.
strings.folders[2].name: Financial records
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: 30-D3 — Approval chain
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body:
Hisham submitted the boundaries. Lama indexed the old title document. Qais approved the beneficiary change under “authorization to follow.” Marwan flagged it for suspension and review.

The company register records a share in Al-Sanad held by Qais’s wife. This does not prove murder and may justify a separate financial inquiry. The missing authorization concerns property 218; the boundary error and family file are separate matters.
strings.folders[3].name: Statements
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: 30-D4 — Supplementary statement: Qais
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body:
Shown 30-E5, Qais said: “Perhaps Marwan put it in my folder as he passed the waiting room. I cannot be certain when.”

Asked about his earlier claim that the folder stayed closed since 18:10, he replied: “I was confused.”

He provided no witness to the encounter. A changed statement is not a confession; test it against the recordings and the document’s chain of custody.
strings.folders[4].name: Verification
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: 30-D5 — Surveyor’s video call
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: From 19:41 to 19:48, Hisham appears continuously on an archived video call from the western survey station, holding up physical maps at the committee’s request. Neither his face nor voice drops out. The call clock matches the reference, and station footage confirms he did not leave during those minutes. There is no absence in which a trip to the eastern wing could fit.
strings.reports[0].title: 30-R1 — Medical examiner’s summary
strings.reports[0].author: Forensic medicine unit
strings.reports[0].body:
Fatal blunt injury resulting from an assault with a solid object. The injury pattern is inconsistent with an accidental fall. The recovered stamp holder’s shape is consistent with the injury, but medical examination cannot identify its user.

Broad medical interval: 19:30–19:50. Examination alone cannot identify a particular minute. Any narrower interval must rely on independently established events; a broad medical estimate must not be presented as an exact time.
strings.reports[1].title: 30-R2 — Recording integrity
strings.reports[1].author: Recording examination unit
strings.reports[1].body:
Both original recordings are continuous throughout the cited intervals, without evidence of cuts or insertions. The corridor clock offset remains constant between the two lamp tests; its frame timestamps have not been altered.

The reception camera and telephone exchange clock agree with the reference. Movement logs and both test records are supplied unchanged. A suspect’s assertion is not a calibration. This report does not identify the culprit; doing so requires linking the recordings to the other evidence.
